concerns.text: Tasks T042-T048 (Reviewer Resolution) implement metrics (Truthfulness Penalty, Behavioral Adaptation, Computational Irreducibility) and falsification logic not defined in spec.md FR-001..FR-007 or SC-001..SC-005. This violates the Single Source of Truth (Constitution Principle IV) and introduces unbounded scope creep. The spec explicitly limits operationalization to self-consistency, calibration, and error detection.

Tasks T004-PLAN and T012-PLAN instruct the implementer to edit `spec.md` and `plan.md` directly to fix placeholders and contradictions. This violates Constitution Principle V (Versioning Discipline) and standard engineering practice; source artifacts must be corrected *before* task generation, not as a task deliverable. Tasks should assume the spec/plan are already consistent.

Task T004-PLAN mandates replacing `[deferred]` in FR-002 with `100000`. While the value is likely correct, the task itself violates the 'sanctioned [deferred] markers' convention (spec 020/023) which states planning docs should defer unverified empirical values. The spec's `[deferred]` is intentional; the task forces a specific value without a research-stage validation step, potentially violating the 'research prediction vs system requirement' distinction in spec.md Assumptions.

Task T045 implements a 'Falsification Criterion' (p < 0.05) to output a binary 'Falsified' status. Spec.md SC-004 and FR-005 only require reporting p-values and effect sizes; they do not define a threshold for 'falsification' or require the system to output a binary status. This task adds an unrequested success criterion and alters the output contract defined in the spec.

Task T048 requires training a separate 'predictor model' for the Computational Irreducibility Test. Spec.md FR-002 only mandates training the recursive and baseline models. This introduces a new model training loop and compute cost not defined in the spec, violating the Resource-Constrained Architectural Fidelity (Constitution Principle VII) and scope boundaries.
